description: Check whether an IP address falls inside each CIDR range you send (allow lists, firewall rules, security groups, VPC subnets). Send one IPv4 or IPv6 address and up to 100 ranges such as 10.0.0.0/8 or 2001:db8::/32. Get back, per range: inside or not, the network, the netmask (IPv4), the broadcast address (IPv4), the first and last usable address, the total and usable address counts, and a flag when the range was written with host bits set (10.0.0.5/24 means 10.0.0.0/24); plus every range that matches and the most specific one (longest prefix). IPv4 /31 and /32 are handled the way RFC 3021 and routers do; IPv6 has no broadcast address. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/cidr-contains). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

cidrs.description: The ranges to test the address against (1 to 100), IPv4 or IPv6, in any mix.

items.description: A range as address/prefix length, such as 192.168.1.0/24 or 2001:db8::/32.

ip.description: The address to test, such as 192.168.1.130 or 2001:db8::1 (no zone ID, no port).
